execution_overview.overall_summary: Built a Python Docker environment and executed Task1 (partial correlations controlling for Age) and Task2 (MiniK group Mann-Whitney U). Both tasks ran successfully and showed that slower life history (higher MiniK/HKSS) is associated with lower psychopathology (DSM5_Total), supporting the focal relationship.

method_fidelity.fidelity_note: Executed the planned partial correlation analyses using the specified dataset and control (Age).

test_statistics.other: DSM5 vs HKSS partial r=-0.4088, t=-5.204, df=135, p=7.09e-07

result_raw.result_text: DSM5_Total is negatively associated with MiniK_Total when controlling for Age (r_partial = -0.513, p < 0.001). A similar negative partial correlation is observed with HKSS_Total.

conclusion.conclusion_text: Results support the claim: higher (slower) life history scores are associated with lower psychopathology after controlling for age.

method_fidelity.fidelity_note: Used the specified MiniK thresholds (fast <= -1; slow >= 1) and executed Levene, Shapiro-Wilk, and Mann-Whitney U tests as planned.

test_statistics.other: Group Ns: fast=16, slow=120; medians: fast=60.5, slow=33.0; Levene F=0.282, p=0.596; Shapiro fast W=0.975, p=0.906; Shapiro slow W=0.846, p<1e-9

result_raw.result_text: DSM5_Total is significantly lower in the slow MiniK group (median 33.0) than in the fast group (median 60.5), U=1671.0, p<0.001.

conclusion.conclusion_text: Results support the claim: those with slower life history (higher MiniK) show lower psychopathology compared to the fast group.
